passages.text: Overexposure to loud music for long durations can cause damage to the ear, resulting in temporary or permanent loss of hearing.
Noise-induced hearing loss is the term that refers to hearing loss that occurs due to exposure to loud noise.
This article will discuss hearing loss due to headphones, signs of hearing loss, and ways to prevent it.

Noise-induced hearing loss is the second most common type of sensorineural hearing loss after age-related hearing loss. A 2017 study indicated that approximately 80% of individuals between 13 and 18 years of age use headphones for listening to music for 1–3 hours a day.
passages.heading_path: Do headphones cause hearing loss?

passages.text: Listening to loud noise for long periods causes hearing loss. This causes damage to the auditory nerve and hair cells of the cochlea, or inner ear.
passages.heading_path: Do headphones cause hearing loss?

passages.text: According to the 2021 study , approximately 1.7% of people worldwide experience noise-induced hearing loss. The study reported individuals who use headphones in an already noisy environment are at a 4.5-fold higher risk of hearing loss.
passages.heading_path: Do headphones cause hearing loss?

passages.text: The recommended sound exposure level is 85 decibels (dBA) for 8 hours a day.
passages.heading_path: Do headphones cause hearing loss?

passages.text: Long or repeated exposure to sounds at or above 85 dBA can cause hearing loss.
passages.heading_path: Do headphones cause hearing loss?

passages.text: Health experts suggest even listening to headphones at a moderate volume can damage hearing over time. It is not just the loudness that causes damage, but the length of exposure.
passages.heading_path: Do headphones cause hearing loss?

passages.text: A few common warning signs of hearing loss include:
passages.heading_path: Warning signs of hearing loss

passages.text: hearing muffled sounds
passages.heading_path: Warning signs of hearing loss

passages.text: difficulty in understanding conversations in noisy places
passages.heading_path: Warning signs of hearing loss

passages.text: difficulty in hearing high-pitch sounds
passages.heading_path: Warning signs of hearing loss

passages.text: difficulty in hearing speech consonants
passages.heading_path: Warning signs of hearing loss

passages.text: ringing in ears
passages.heading_path: Warning signs of hearing loss

passages.text: asking someone to repeat what they said or speak loudly
passages.heading_path: Warning signs of hearing loss

passages.text: hypersensitivity to certain sounds
passages.heading_path: Warning signs of hearing loss

passages.text: People who have any of the above symptoms should consult a doctor. People may receive a referral to a hearing doctor .
passages.heading_path: Warning signs of hearing loss

passages.text: Screening for hearing loss is a fairly simple and painless procedure.
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss

passages.text: If someone suspects hearing loss, the doctor will first perform a physical examination of the ear, known as an otoscopy. This procedure examines the structures of the ear, such as:
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss

passages.text: The external auditory canal: The ear canal moves sound toward the eardrum, known as the tympanic membrane.
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss
passages.speaker: The external auditory canal

passages.text: The tympanic membrane: A thin membrane that performs two functions: transmission and amplification.
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss
passages.speaker: The tympanic membrane

passages.text: The middle ear: This part of the ear connects external sound waves with the the inner ear for auditory transduction — conversion of sound to an electrical waveform.
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss
passages.speaker: The middle ear

passages.text: During the screening, a doctor may ask a person to cover one ear and describe what they can hear at different volumes. The doctor will also check their sensitivity to certain sounds.
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss > General screening test

passages.text: If the doctor suspects a hearing problem, they will refer a person to an ear, nose, and throat (ENT) specialist or an audiologist. They may carry out further testing, such as:
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss > General screening test

passages.text: A tuning fork test: This test uses a metal instrument that vibrates against the ear from different distances. This will help determine when a person can no longer hear a sound.
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss > General screening test
passages.speaker: A tuning fork test

passages.text: Audiometer test: A person will wear suitably fitted earphones, and doctors will direct sounds at a controlled range of volumes and tones into one ear at a time. Like the above test, an audiologist will ask someone to confirm when they can no longer hear a sound.
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss > General screening test
passages.speaker: Audiometer test

passages.text: Bone oscillator test: This test places an oscillator against the ear bone to determine the nerve’s function and the type of hearing loss a person may have.
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss > General screening test
passages.speaker: Bone oscillator test

passages.text: A person can discuss any concerns relating to the screening or the results with a medical professional. The sooner people receive a diagnosis after experiencing early hearing loss signs, the quicker a doctor can work to reduce the effects of hearing loss or damage may have on their quality of life.
passages.heading_path: Diagnosing hearing issues and loss > General screening test

passages.text: There are several methods doctors can help improve a person’s ability to hear, including:
passages.heading_path: Treating hearing loss

passages.text: hearing aids
passages.heading_path: Treating hearing loss

passages.text: middle ear implants
passages.heading_path: Treating hearing loss

passages.text: cochlear implants
passages.heading_path: Treating hearing loss

passages.text: lip reading and sign language
passages.heading_path: Treating hearing loss

passages.text: A hearing doctor can explore the most suitable option for a person’s noise-induced hearing loss.
passages.heading_path: Treating hearing loss

passages.text: Find out what are the best apps for American Sign Language.
passages.heading_path: Treating hearing loss

passages.text: Some of the approaches to prevent hearing loss with headphones include:
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: turning down the volume of headphones below the recommended level to limit exposure to loud noise
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: using noise-canceling headphones that block out external sound allows people to enjoy their music at low volumes
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: replacing earbuds or in-the-ear headphones with over-the-ear headphones
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: reducing listening times
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: getting routine checkups of ears
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: A person can lower volume levels even when not using headphones, such as on televisions or smartphones, and can use ear protection at loud events or environments.
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: People should consult a doctor if they have any signs of an ear infection , such as:
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: prolonged earache
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: ear discharge
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: worsened or persistent hearing loss
passages.heading_path: Ways to prevent hearing loss with headphones

passages.text: Overuse of headphones may cause permanent hearing loss by damaging the hair cells of the inner ear and the auditory nerve.
passages.heading_path: Summary

passages.text: People must take breaks when using headphones. They should also avoid exposure to noise above recommended levels. A person should consult an ear doctor if they have any warning signs of hearing loss, so they can receive a suitable diagnosis and treatment.

Headphones can play a huge part in our lives. We use them to listen to our favorite music and podcasts, to participate in Zoom calls, and to watch shows or movies. Headphone usage is widespread among different age groups as well. Toddlers, older adults, and everyone in between likely have a pair.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health

passages.text: However, daily headphone use can pose risks to your hearing, including hearing loss, and it’s important to use them responsibly.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health

passages.text: “Hearing damage caused by noise is from a combination of volume and duration,” says Kate Johnson, AuD, CCC-A , an audiologist at University of Utah Health. “The louder the sound, the shorter the amount of time you can be exposed before damage will happen.”
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > The Most Important Factors: Volume and Duration

passages.text: Today’s portable audio devices can get as loud as 120 dBA, which is equivalent to the sound levels at a rock concert. Listening to audio at this level can lead to hearing damage in a matter of seconds.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Volume

passages.text: Audiologists recommend keeping the audio levels at or below 60 percent of the maximum volume . Between 65-85 dBa is considered a safe range. This is equivalent to the volume of typical human speech on the lower end and busy city traffic on the higher end.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Volume

passages.text: Many smartphone apps can measure sound levels, so if you’re concerned about noise exposure, try downloading one to ensure you’re not exceeding the limit.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Volume

passages.text: The length of time you listen through your headphones is also important. If you must use your headphones daily, be sure to take breaks to allow your ears time to recover.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Duration

passages.text: “You can listen to 85 dBA for eight hours without risk of hearing damage,” Johnson says. “For every three-decibel increase, that time is cut in half, so knowing the volume of a sound is the simplest way to know your exposure risk.”
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Duration

passages.text: According to the American Osteopathic Association , hearing loss linked to headphone usage is increasing. About 1 in 5 teenagers will experience some form of hearing damage, which is about 30% higher than it was 20 years ago.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Hearing Loss Symptoms

passages.text: If you are a regular user of headphones and experience any of these symptoms , you might want to consider cutting back and seeing an audiologist:
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Hearing Loss Symptoms

passages.text: Tinnitus, which is a ringing, hissing, or buzzing sound in the ear
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Hearing Loss Symptoms

passages.text: Difficulty hearing in noisy environments
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Hearing Loss Symptoms

passages.text: Difficulty understanding what people are saying
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Hearing Loss Symptoms

passages.text: Needing to watch TV at a higher volume
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Hearing Loss Symptoms

passages.text: “Hearing loss caused by noise exposure is cumulative over a lifetime,” Johnson says. “If temporary hearing changes are noted, it should also be noted that future damage can happen at lowered exposure levels and times.”
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Hearing Loss Symptoms

passages.text: Johnson recommends seeing an audiologist if you are ever concerned about noise-induced hearing loss.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Hearing Loss Symptoms

passages.text: When you’re shopping for your next pair of headphones, you can look for certain factors to ensure you’re choosing a product that is safe for your ears.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Navigating the Headphone Market

passages.text: “Physically, there are no headphones that are safer than others,” Johnson says. “The safety comes from exposure to sound.”
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Navigating the Headphone Market

passages.text: Johnson recommends looking into headphones with noise-cancelling technology. Noise-cancelling headphones can block out external noises, which allows you to listen to music or podcasts at a lower volume.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Navigating the Headphone Market

passages.text: Besides opting for noise-cancelling headphones, these factors can also help you make smart choices for your hearing health:
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Navigating the Headphone Market

passages.text: Volume Control: Some types of headphones allow you to set a maximum volume. You can also limit volume on your devices to ensure you are not listening to anything above the recommended 65-85 dBa.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Navigating the Headphone Market
passages.speaker: Volume Control

passages.text: Limit daily usage: Be mindful of the total time you’re using your headphones each day, and be sure to give your ears regular breaks.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Navigating the Headphone Market
passages.speaker: Limit daily usage

passages.text: Model good behavior: Help protect your kids’ ears by showing them how to use their headphones responsibly.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Navigating the Headphone Market
passages.speaker: Model good behavior

passages.text: While headphones add convenience and enjoyment to our daily lives, being aware of the potential risks to our hearing health and using them responsibly is crucial to keeping our ears happy in the long term.
passages.heading_path: Listen Up: Headphone Use Can Impact Your Hearing Health > Navigating the Headphone Market
